title: Service level
caption: Service level 85-99 %: total safety stock the LP would hold (110 products, SS = Z x sigma_d x sqrt(8 business days), placeholder review/lead days) against expected stockouts. Current Z = 1.28 (lp.py, 90 %): 459,359 pieces. At 85 % / 95 % / 99 %: 371,950 / 590,296 / 834,867 pieces. Model-implied SKU-months with a stockout per year (normal demand, 4.35 independent weekly cycles a month) fall from 669 at 85 % to 56 at 99 %. Measured on the stored rolling one-step holdout (79 of the products, 1730 SKU-months, 2023-10..2026-02, served model by history length): actual demand exceeded forecast + 1.28 x monthly sigma in 9.1% of months (95 % CI 7.9%-10.5%, bootstrap over SKUs) against the nominal 10 %. Sigma is the LP's own: the SKU's monthly demand standard deviation over its whole history (holdout months included), recovered as sigma_d x sqrt(average business days a month).
verdict_detail: measured monthly exceedance at Z=1.28: 9.1% (95% CI 7.9%-10.5%, SKU bootstrap) vs nominal 10%
criterion: Stockout months are labelled model-implied (normal assumption). FLAWED if the measured monthly exceedance (actual > forecast + 1.28 sigma) has a 95% interval entirely above 10% (Z = 1.28 <-> 90%; analytics/optimization/lp.py:14)

checks.detail: run_lp.safety_stock_for at Z=1.28 equals Z x sigma_d x sqrt(8) summed: True

data_notes: LP inputs are PLACEHOLDERS (analytics/params.py PLACEHOLDERS), realistic values the team chose, not SSM's figures: allocation_pct 103, review_days 5, lead_days 3, target_weeks 3, cover_rule aggregate, warehouse_capacity 3.81684e+06, default_procurement_cost_per_unit 33.48, storage_cost_per_unit 0.5.
Pool: Category A with a stored forecast of status 'ok' and MASE < 1 (pipeline gate).
The model-implied stockout months are a formula (normal demand, independent weekly cycles), not a measurement; the measured exceedance is at monthly grain.
